question: How many languages is the Best Practices Guide available in?

sentences:
In this document, security and compliance is considered from the perspective of the [National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF)](https://). The CSF is a set of voluntary guidelines, standards, and practices made available by NIST, an agency of the United States Department of Commerce.

This Best Practices Guide is also available in the following languages: [Spanish](https://), [French](https://), [German](https://), [Dutch](https://), [Italian](https://), [Brazilian Portuguese](https://), [Korean](https://), and [Japanese](https://).

---

Note: All information in this white paper is related to the standard ServiceNow Commercial Cloud.

For information related to other globally located ServiceNow in-country cloud offerings and how these offerings may differ, please contact your ServiceNow account representative.

---

November 2025 | Release: Zurich
```

```markdown
# Penetration testing

## Customer responsibility
Customers may perform application [penetration testing](#) against their sub-production instance(s) in accordance with the ServiceNow Customer Penetration Testing Policy. (Link requires a ServiceNow Support account.)

## ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow performs nightly web application security testing using automated and manual techniques, along with third-party security scanning tools.

This process ensures that security assessments are integrated during code development. Findings identified during testing are reviewed by the ServiceNow Product Security Team and forwarded to development for remediation.

Prior to each major release (twice per year), ServiceNow engages an independent third-party to conduct comprehensive application penetration testing using industry-standard methodologies.

```markdown
# RESPOND

## Incident management

### Customer responsibility
During an incident, customers must lead investigations based on their internal processes, security needs, and regulatory obligations, as ServiceNow cannot anticipate these specifics. In addition, ServiceNow asks that customers keep their security contacts updated in the event that ServiceNow needs to reach out for a suspected incident.

While ServiceNow can assist with questions on the investigation, customers are responsible for classifying related behavior as malicious or benign, given their contextual knowledge. [ServiceNow Support](#) can help interpret log samples but cannot review all logs or determine the full scope of an incident.

To ensure effective assistance, customers are responsible for providing detailed information—such as timelines, IPs, and user data—when requesting support. Broad log queries can delay investigations, whereas targeted data enables faster resolution.

```markdown
# Best practices continued

## Limit concurrent sessions
Work with your security team to determine if you need to [limit concurrent sessions](#) for the same concurrent interactive sessions to reduce the risk of session hijacking or credential abuse.

## Evaluate adaptive authentication with Session Validation Context
Evaluate the adaptive authentication’s [Session Validation Context](#) to automatically end user sessions if the session’s IP address changes unexpectedly. This approach helps maintain security by ensuring that only users accessing from their original network context can continue their sessions.

## Activate default deny with High security plugin
The [High security plugin (HSP)](#) is installed and enabled by default on all new ServiceNow instances. Customers can set a [default deny property](#), which prevents read, write, create, and delete for all tables, unless explicit permission is given for a user or role in an ACL rule. Verify the plugin is enabled.

## Best practices continued

### Monitor and forward logs to the organization’s SIEM for threat detection
To enhance threat detection and response, organizations should actively monitor and forward relevant log data from their ServiceNow instance to a SIEM following internal security policies.

### Enable Protected Tables plugin to manage log tampering
Customers should ensure the Protected Tables plugin is enabled on their ServiceNow instance and the protection levels are set. When the `com.glide.security.protected_table.enabled` property is set to true, the protected tables plugin will be used to prevent higher privilege users on an instance from tampering with log tables. Collaborate with the organization’s security team to review and set appropriate protection levels and actions and add specific alerts that may need to be added to monitoring procedures.

```markdown
# GOVERN

## Security contacts

**Customer responsibility**  
As outlined in the DSA, customers are responsible for identifying and maintaining appropriate security contacts by identifying them in [ServiceNow Support Security Contacts](https://www.servicenow.com).

**Best practices**  

### Create a process to update security contacts regularly  
Ensure the security contact record within ServiceNow Support is always kept up to date, with details of at least two appropriate information security personnel. Set a reminder to review the security contact details at least quarterly to ensure they are current and accurate.  

- Security contacts should be authorized to act on the information they receive, because it may be critically important to the organization.  
- Use a distribution list in the security contact field when possible.  

**Additional information**  
- Update your [ServiceNow Support Security Contacts](https://www.servicenow.com) (requires a ServiceNow Support account)

---

```markdown

Use ServiceNow Access Analyzer to conduct regular audits of user, group, and role permissions for core platform elements such as tables, script includes, UI pages, and REST endpoints. question: What can trigger an account lockout in ServiceNow?

sentences:
#### Configure and enforce strong password policies
It is important for customers to set password policies for their Identity Provider (IdP) and within their ServiceNow instance(s). This includes specifying requirements like minimum password length, complexity, expiration, uniqueness, and lockout conditions for native accounts. Also, be sure configurations meet your organizational standards.

#### Enable account lockout to prevent brute force attacks
As a critical security best practice, customers should enable account lockouts both on their IdP and for all local accounts within the ServiceNow instance. This measure is essential to defend against brute force authentication attacks by automatically locking accounts after a set number of failed login attempts.

### Review event logs to detect unauthorized access and privilege escalation
Regularly review event logs for login activity and privilege escalation to identify and respond to potential security threats. Event logs provide insights into system activity, including successful and failed login attempts and privilege escalation events.

### Monitor system logs for configuration changes and errors
Routinely monitor system logs to detect configuration changes, system errors, and unusual data connections that may indicate security or operational issues. System logs contain information about general activity, including configuration changes, system errors, workflows, and inbound/outbound data connections.

### Review transaction logs to detect malicious web activity
Review transaction logs to identify unusual or malicious web activity, as they provide records of all browser-based interactions with the ServiceNow instance.

```markdown
# Compliance: Regulatory and legal  
## Data Security Addendum (DSA) and Data Processing Addendum (DPA)  

### Customer responsibility  
Customers need to be aware that the terms and conditions governing the use of the ServiceNow AI Platform are dependent on their order form agreement with ServiceNow, including matters of data security and privacy.  

The [Data Security Addendum (DSA)](https://www.servicenow.com) covers key aspects of the ServiceNow security program: certifications and attestations, logging and monitoring, change control, and access administration, as well as other compliance and governance details.  

The [Data Processing Addendum (DPA)](https://www.servicenow.com) reflects the customer's agreement regarding personal data. The DPA also defines the roles of the **data controller** and **data processor**, and describes the nature, scope, and purpose of the processing.

#### Use the completed questionnaires in the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal to support due diligence efforts
Use the ServiceNow pre-completed Consensus Assessment Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ) and Standardized Information Gathering (SIG) questionnaire to simplify your evaluation process. (Links require access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#).) These resources save time, speed up risk assessments, and help stakeholders quickly find key details for audits. For any questions, our account teams are available to assist promptly.

## Instance management

### Customer responsibility
Customers must oversee all the organization’s production and sub-production ServiceNow instances, ensuring each one’s purpose, owner, and data classification are known.

### Best practices

#### Maintain a centralized inventory of instances
Maintain a centralized, up-to-date inventory of all ServiceNow instances (see the [ServiceNow Support Instances Dashboard](#)). Clearly identify each instance by name and URL, environment type (such as Production, Development, Test, or Sandbox), business purpose, designated business and technical owners, and data classification.

Conduct regular reviews of all production and sub-production ServiceNow instances to verify each instance’s ownership, purpose, and ongoing alignment with business needs. Document each review and its findings and formalize the follow-up process to support continuous oversight.

# Encryption
## Data in transit

### Customer responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform provides customers with encryption in transit via HTTPS for user access and API access to the instance. The platform also supports several protocols for integration with customer or third-party systems, including HTTPS, LDAPS, FTPS, and SCP. Customers should configure data in transit encryption methods in accordance with their security policies and use cases.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform supports default encryption in transit for sessions inbound to the instance using a minimum of TLS 1.2. All attempted access to a ServiceNow instance over HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

ServiceNow instance email infrastructure supports opportunistic TLS for sending or receiving email.

---

### Best practices

#### Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for browser connections
Customer admins should configure their web browsers to use only TLS 1.2, or higher when connecting to their ServiceNow instance.

# Best practices

## Understand the ServiceNow Data Sharing Program
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to fully understand how anonymized data is shared with ServiceNow. Confirm the intended data contribution strategy with appropriate stakeholders. Customers of the Advanced AI and Data Products can opt out of sharing data.

Refer to the [Data Sharing Programs](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=b16448406) and [AI Model Improvement](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=b16448406) for details on how ServiceNow collects and uses customer-contributed data to enhance AI models, as per the [product-specific terms](https://www.servicenow.com/store).

- Customers can opt out of anonymized data sharing within 30 days of downloading an AI app from the [ServiceNow Store](https://www.servicenow.com/store).
- Data sharing for the Advanced AI and Data Products can be managed from the Now Assist Admin Console.

# Encryption
## Data in transit

### Customer responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform provides customers with encryption in transit via HTTPS for user access and API access to the instance. The platform also supports several protocols for integration with customer or third-party systems, including HTTPS, LDAPS, FTPS, and SCP. Customers should configure data in transit encryption methods in accordance with their security policies and use cases.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform supports default encryption in transit for sessions inbound to the instance using a minimum of TLS 1.2. All attempted access to a ServiceNow instance over HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

ServiceNow instance email infrastructure supports opportunistic TLS for sending or receiving email.

---

### Best practices

#### Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for browser connections
Customer admins should configure their web browsers to use only TLS 1.2, or higher when connecting to their ServiceNow instance.</DOCUMENT>

**Platform Encryption Bundle**: Combines Field Encryption Enterprise, Cloud Encryption, and the Key Management Framework (KMF) for comprehensive encryption coverage.

### Best practices

#### Ensure key stakeholders have access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal
Establish a formal procedure to identify relevant parties, including compliance teams, vendor risk assessment teams, and security personnel who require access to CORE documentation for internal audits and vendor evaluations, and provide them with the necessary portal access.

#### Periodically review the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal
Establish a process involving relevant stakeholders to conduct regular reviews of CORE content and implement a method for collecting and addressing clarification questions following material review.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>ServiceNow has separate business continuity plans and processes, which are tested annually, in place to ensure availability for the ServiceNow corporate organization and the services it relies on.

#### Advanced High Availability (AHA) architecture
ServiceNow colocation facilities are arranged in regional pairs, with all customer production data hosted in both colocation facilities simultaneously. ServiceNow uses asynchronous database replication to keep these pairs in sync.

When performing maintenance, or if an infrastructure component fails, transfer between active and passive colocation facilities is executed as part of ServiceNow standard operating procedures. This ensures that when AHA is needed to address an instance failure, the transfer will be successful and service disruption minimized.</DOCUMENT>

# ServiceNow responsibility continued

## Backup restoration
If a customer deletes data inadvertently, or if a customer's data integration or automation gets misconfigured or malfunctions, this could render data unusable or inaccessible. In these scenarios, AHA architecture would not be able to recover the deleted data or data loss due to misconfiguration, because with AHA database replication occurs to both instances in the pair at near real-time. Restoring from **backup** is the only option for recovery.

ServiceNow can restore customer data upon request. For more information, see the [ServiceNow Backup and Restoration SOP](#) (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#)).

## Media disposal and destruction
Media disposal and destruction refers to the disposal of hard drives in ServiceNow colocation facilities. ServiceNow follows NIST 800-88 guidelines for destroying hard drives and rendering the media infeasible for future use.

# Best practices continued

## Understand the goal of ServiceNow Security Center metrics
Built-in security metrics in the Security Center provide data on potential threats and trends, allowing users to observe key indicators and set up alerts. These metrics and dashboards are primarily intended for raising awareness rather than continuous monitoring. Organizations with more advanced needs can integrate a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) solution for real-time tracking and automated response. It is important to assess whether SIEM integration is necessary for your organization’s security team to enhance the capabilities provided by Security Center metrics. For detailed guidance on SIEM integration, refer to the [logging and monitoring section](#).

## Review and complete customer actions promptly
Increase your instance’s security posture by ensuring that system-recommended Customer Actions are implemented on time.

### Monitor antivirus queues for malicious uploads
Customers should establish a defined process for monitoring uploaded file attachments for potential malicious content, leveraging anti-virus scanning capabilities in the platform. This process should include ongoing collaboration with security teams to analyze, identify, and respond to emerging patterns or trends in suspicious uploads, ensuring proactive protection of the instance and its data.

### Configure inbound REST API rate limiting
Set rules to limit inbound REST API requests. Customers can create rules that limit the number of inbound REST API requests processed per hour and can also create rules to limit requests for specific users, users with specific roles, or all users.

### Review public REST API endpoints
Review the identified REST API endpoint and use cases. Determine if unauthenticated users should be allowed access.

```markdown
# Best practices continued

## Implement logging and monitoring for the MID Server
Please review the specific logging and monitoring considerations below related to the MID Server and the [logging and monitoring section](#). Collaborate with stakeholders to develop a comprehensive logging and monitoring strategy.

- Consider enabling the MID Server Command Audit Log to track all executed commands.
- Monitor changes to sensitive roles (e.g., `discovery_admin`, `mid_server`) and alert on unauthorized modifications.
- Forward all log data to your internal SIEM platform for correlation and analysis. For detailed guidance on SIEM integration, refer to the [logging and monitoring section](#).

---

*Note*: Security data filters may impact system performance and slow query and page load times, if not used carefully.

## Use Contextual Security Manager to evaluate table access when possible
The Contextual Security Manager works alongside the broader security framework at ServiceNow, which includes ACLs that can be applied to individual records and fields within tables. This allows for much more sophisticated access control than simple role-based permissions. The plugin is particularly useful when you need security rules that depend on the specific circumstances of the access request rather than just the user’s assigned roles. ### Enable table auditing for complete record history
Customers can enable auditing for database tables, making record history perpetual and allowing tracking of any changes made to the data since creation. By default, only the incident, problem, and change tables are tracked. For other tables, auditing must be enabled manually.

### Review import logs to ensure data integrity
Regularly review import logs to track data import activity, including source, status, and timing, to ensure data integrity and detect any anomalies.

### Use API Analytics to track inbound API usage
Use API Analytics to monitor inbound API usage and users. Customers can track and analyze inbound REST and SOAP activity with API Analytics. These analytics help customers understand which APIs are being used, by whom, and to what degree.

sentences:
```markdown
# Authorization

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for defining user roles based on job functions and assigning appropriate permissions using role-based access control (RBAC) and access control lists (ACLs). It is recommended to configure ACLs to enforce the principle of least privilege and use non-production instances to test changes before deployment.

---

## Best practices

### Distinguish between interactive vs non-interactive user accounts
**Interactive user accounts** should use MFA and role-based access controls, ensuring least privilege and tying actions to individuals for accountability.

**Non-interactive accounts**, intended for integrations and automation, should authenticate via API keys or OAuth tokens, have roles restricted to their purpose, utilize IP restrictions when possible, and link actions to the system or team.

```markdown
### Best practices continued

#### Understand Account recovery (ACR) capabilities
When utilizing Single Sign-On (SSO), ensure that at least one Account Recovery (ACR) administrator is registered prior to activation. This precaution secures fallback access to critical systems should primary authentication methods become misconfigured or unavailable. Thoroughly document all ACR procedures, limit access strictly to authorized personnel, and regularly audit ACR usage to uphold strong security standards. Restrict local logins for interactive sessions to approved recovery users with MFA enabled and employ ACR solely as a recovery tool to maintain system integrity.

### Refer developers to the Secure Coding Guide
Always adhere to secure coding best practices when developing applications. The [Secure Coding Guide](https://www.servicenow.com/) provides detailed recommendations on topics such as input/output sanitization, session management, secure access, and more (link requires a ServiceNow Support account).

Customers are responsible for ensuring the security of the MID Server by maintaining strict physical controls, deploying and hardening the server and operating system in accordance with their internal IT policies, and restricting network access to only essential services and infrastructure. They are also responsible for operating the MID Server and managing account credentials. Additionally, customers must monitor firewall and proxy configurations to allow only the necessary connections.

---

## Best practices

### Secure physical access to the MID Server
Place the MID Server in a physically secure location, such as a locked data center or server room, with access restricted to authorized personnel. Follow your organization’s access audit requirements to detect and prevent unauthorized entry.

For integration accounts, enable the web services access flag to prevent those accounts from using interactive sessions.

### Define roles clearly
Identify each job function that will interact with the ServiceNow AI Platform and assign specific user roles with clear names and descriptions. Update roles as business needs evolve and communicate privileges to users. Adopt the concept of least-privileged access. This ensures effective access control and simplifies auditing.

#### Align with change management
Changes to ServiceNow instances should follow the organization’s change management process. Document each activity with an official record and obtain approvals before proceeding to ensure tracking, authorization, and compliance.

#### Plan for acceptable use
Customers should work with all stakeholders to define appropriate usage guidelines for ServiceNow. This guidance should be published in the organizational standards, when appropriate. Manage instance activity in accordance with company guidelines throughout each instance’s lifecycle.

#### Retire unused instances
Decommission ServiceNow instances that are no longer needed, following the organization’s documented retirement process that includes backing up critical data, removing all integrations and credentials, and updating the centralized inventory to reflect changes.

- [Requesting instance retire via service catalog on ServiceNow Support](#) (requires a ServiceNow Support account)

## Understand how to review logs for investigations
One of the most important components of incident response is ServiceNow instance logs. These [system logs](https://support.servicenow.com), will be able to provide customers’ security teams with the necessary telemetry for their incident response investigations. Logs can be reviewed using a variety of methods, such as the [log file browser](https://support.servicenow.com), Table APIs, and directly in the platform.

## Conduct postmortem activities following a security incident
Following a security incident, it is important to perform a postmortem review of the investigations to determine possible improvements that can be made for future incident response activities. This can include identifying possible communication issues, gaps within the environment’s security posture, and ensuring all involved parties understand the root cause of the issue and how to avoid similar situations moving forward.

Work with your security team to determine if you need to [limit concurrent sessions](#) for the same concurrent interactive sessions to reduce the risk of session hijacking or credential abuse.

## Evaluate adaptive authentication with Session Validation Context
Evaluate the adaptive authentication’s [Session Validation Context](#) to automatically end user sessions if the session’s IP address changes unexpectedly. This approach helps maintain security by ensuring that only users accessing from their original network context can continue their sessions.

## Activate default deny with High security plugin
The [High security plugin (HSP)](#) is installed and enabled by default on all new ServiceNow instances. # Request that the support case be marked as a security case
If a case being submitted involves confirmed compromise of customer information, customers are able to request the case be flagged as a security case, which limits the case visibility as needed. Ensure that security cases are intentionally designated as such. Customer visibility into a security case is limited to the submitter and any accounts designated on the case’s watchlist.

## Educate your security team on how to raise a case with ServiceNow Support
Ensure that your security team, or at a minimum, the designated security contact in [Security Contacts on ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com), has documentation on how to create a support case via [support.servicenow.com](https://support.servicenow.com) in the event they need to report an incident and cannot contact a member of the platform team.

## Enable automatic account creation only when necessary
Automatic account creation allows user accounts to be [created dynamically by email](#). This feature should be used with care. Activate this feature if necessary for a specific use case. Regularly review whether this feature is still needed and disable if not.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system to review and correlate logs from multiple network and infrastructure sources. A Scheduled Security Operations Checklist is in place, which includes daily reviews of:
- Linux and Windows systems  
- Network devices  
- Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts  
- Behavioral and identified issue logs  

High-risk issues, such as intrusion detection events, trigger real-time alerts that are immediately sent to the Security Incident Response Team for review. Network and infrastructure log events are retained for a minimum of 90 days.

---

### Best practices

## Instance management

### Customer responsibility
Customers must oversee all the organization’s production and sub-production ServiceNow instances, ensuring each one’s purpose, owner, and data classification are known.

### Best practices

#### Maintain a centralized inventory of instances
Maintain a centralized, up-to-date inventory of all ServiceNow instances (see the [ServiceNow Support Instances Dashboard](#)). Clearly identify each instance by name and URL, environment type (such as Production, Development, Test, or Sandbox), business purpose, designated business and technical owners, and data classification.

#### Regularly review all instances
Conduct regular reviews of all production and sub-production ServiceNow instances to verify each instance’s ownership, purpose, and ongoing alignment with business needs. Document each review and its findings and formalize the follow-up process to support continuous oversight.

ServiceNow has separate business continuity plans and processes, which are tested annually, in place to ensure availability for the ServiceNow corporate organization and the services it relies on.

#### Advanced High Availability (AHA) architecture
ServiceNow colocation facilities are arranged in regional pairs, with all customer production data hosted in both colocation facilities simultaneously. ServiceNow uses asynchronous database replication to keep these pairs in sync.

When performing maintenance, or if an infrastructure component fails, transfer between active and passive colocation facilities is executed as part of ServiceNow standard operating procedures. This ensures that when AHA is needed to address an instance failure, the transfer will be successful and service disruption minimized.

---

Establish a formal procedure to identify relevant parties, including compliance teams, vendor risk assessment teams, and security personnel who require access to CORE documentation for internal audits and vendor evaluations, and provide them with the necessary portal access.

Establish a process involving relevant stakeholders to conduct regular reviews of CORE content and implement a method for collecting and addressing clarification questions following material review.

# ServiceNow responsibility continued

## Backup restoration
If a customer deletes data inadvertently, or if a customer's data integration or automation gets misconfigured or malfunctions, this could render data unusable or inaccessible. In these scenarios, AHA architecture would not be able to recover the deleted data or data loss due to misconfiguration, because with AHA database replication occurs to both instances in the pair at near real-time. Restoring from **backup** is the only option for recovery.

ServiceNow can restore customer data upon request. For more information, see the [ServiceNow Backup and Restoration SOP](#) (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#)).

## Media disposal and destruction
Media disposal and destruction refers to the disposal of hard drives in ServiceNow colocation facilities. ServiceNow follows NIST 800-88 guidelines for destroying hard drives and rendering the media infeasible for future use.

---

```markdown
# Data at rest

## Customer responsibility

# ServiceNow responsibility continued

## Backup restoration
If a customer deletes data inadvertently, or if a customer's data integration or automation gets misconfigured or malfunctions, this could render data unusable or inaccessible. In these scenarios, AHA architecture would not be able to recover the deleted data or data loss due to misconfiguration, because with AHA database replication occurs to both instances in the pair at near real-time. Restoring from **backup** is the only option for recovery.

ServiceNow can restore customer data upon request. For more information, see the [ServiceNow Backup and Restoration SOP](#) (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#)).

Media disposal and destruction refers to the disposal of hard drives in ServiceNow colocation facilities. ServiceNow follows NIST 800-88 guidelines for destroying hard drives and rendering the media infeasible for future use.

#### Align with change management
Changes to ServiceNow instances should follow the organization’s change management process. Document each activity with an official record and obtain approvals before proceeding to ensure tracking, authorization, and compliance.

#### Plan for acceptable use
Customers should work with all stakeholders to define appropriate usage guidelines for ServiceNow. This guidance should be published in the organizational standards, when appropriate. Manage instance activity in accordance with company guidelines throughout each instance’s lifecycle.

#### Retire unused instances
Decommission ServiceNow instances that are no longer needed, following the organization’s documented retirement process that includes backing up critical data, removing all integrations and credentials, and updating the centralized inventory to reflect changes.

Customers should ensure that the [protected tables plugin](#) is enabled on their ServiceNow instance and that appropriate protection levels are configured. When the property `com.glide.security.protected_table.enabled` is set to true, the platform applies controls designed to prevent privileged users from tampering with critical log tables. This capability is essential for maintaining the integrity of audit data and reducing the risk of unauthorized changes.  

To implement protected tables effectively, security teams should review and define the correct protection levels and actions that align with their company policies. It is equally important to incorporate alerts into monitoring procedures so that any attempt to modify protected tables is detected promptly.  

By combining these measures, organizations can strengthen compliance, preserve operational transparency, and ensure that sensitive log data remains secure throughout its lifecycle.

#### Address noncompliance with security hardening and hardening compliance score
Use [Security hardening](https://www.servicenow.com) to identify, test, and assess noncompliance in a sub-production instance. Review the hardening compliance score to determine how closely your instance aligns with SSC hardening recommendations.

As a security best practice, organizations should collaborate with security and compliance teams to identify which ServiceNow instances require penetration testing and establish a clear process for these assessments. ### Customer responsibility
While ServiceNow manages infrastructure-level disaster recovery and system failover, customers should create and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans tailored to their processes and risk tolerance for their ServiceNow instance. By proactively addressing these responsibilities, customers help ensure their organization is prepared to respond quickly and effectively in the event of an unexpected disruption.

ServiceNow operates a disaster recovery program for customer instances called the [Information System Contingency Plan (ISCP)](https://www.servicenow.com/). (Link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](https://www.servicenow.com/).)

sentences:
```markdown
# The Shared Responsibility Model

Security is a partnership between ServiceNow and the customer, both with specific responsibilities. Therefore, it is essential that each party understands their role in this partnership. Using the extensive capabilities of the ServiceNow AI Platform, customers can configure instances to meet their unique security policies and obligations while also complying with any regional or industry-specific requirements.

- **As the data controller**, the customer determines access rights to their instance and the data it contains. Security controls within the instance enable customers to implement policies appropriate to their own requirements and make decisions on data classification.

- **As the data processor**, ServiceNow secures the platform infrastructure and provides tools for security management and monitoring according to customer requirements.

#### Assess whether local login requires restrictions
Collaborate with stakeholders, including IT, security, and business leaders, to evaluate whether local login methods should be restricted for interactive sessions. Consider potential risks, operational requirements, and integration needs.

---

November 2025 | Release: Zurich
```

```markdown
# Authorization

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for defining user roles based on job functions and assigning appropriate permissions using role-based access control (RBAC) and access control lists (ACLs). It is recommended to configure ACLs to enforce the principle of least privilege and use non-production instances to test changes before deployment.

---

## Best practices

### Distinguish between interactive vs non-interactive user accounts
**Interactive user accounts** should use MFA and role-based access controls, ensuring least privilege and tying actions to individuals for accountability.

**Non-interactive accounts**, intended for integrations and automation, should authenticate via API keys or OAuth tokens, have roles restricted to their purpose, utilize IP restrictions when possible, and link actions to the system or team.

```markdown
# Best practices

## Understand the ServiceNow Data Sharing Program
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to fully understand how anonymized data is shared with ServiceNow. Confirm the intended data contribution strategy with appropriate stakeholders. Customers of the Advanced AI and Data Products can opt out of sharing data.

Refer to the [Data Sharing Programs](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=b16448406) and [AI Model Improvement](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=b16448406) for details on how ServiceNow collects and uses customer-contributed data to enhance AI models, as per the [product-specific terms](https://www.servicenow.com/store).

- Customers can opt out of anonymized data sharing within 30 days of downloading an AI app from the [ServiceNow Store](https://www.servicenow.com/store).
- Data sharing for the Advanced AI and Data Products can be managed from the Now Assist Admin Console.

sentences:
## Use Contextual Security Manager to evaluate table access when possible
The Contextual Security Manager works alongside the broader security framework at ServiceNow, which includes ACLs that can be applied to individual records and fields within tables. This allows for much more sophisticated access control than simple role-based permissions. The plugin is particularly useful when you need security rules that depend on the specific circumstances of the access request rather than just the user’s assigned roles. This makes it valuable for complex enterprise environments where access requirements vary based on data context, business rules, or dynamic conditions.

```

It is recommended that customers limit the use of personal identities for executing unattended automations or integrations. By implementing ServiceNow access policy restrictions to clearly separate these data flows, organizations can better define and uphold policies aligned with their identity architecture.

### Use security attributes when possible
Customers should utilize applicable security attributes when possible. Security attributes offer an alternative method for access control via role definitions.

### Use security data filters when possible
Security data filters enable access restriction to records based on a user’s role, or other security attribute-related assertions. Security data filters are applied before a query is executed and ensure only authorized users can view records regardless of how data is accessed. Customers should explicitly enable security data filters for user-facing queries that are not using GlideRecordSecure.

Customers should ensure that the [protected tables plugin](#) is enabled on their ServiceNow instance and that appropriate protection levels are configured. When the property `com.glide.security.protected_table.enabled` is set to true, the platform applies controls designed to prevent privileged users from tampering with critical log tables. This capability is essential for maintaining the integrity of audit data and reducing the risk of unauthorized changes.  

To implement protected tables effectively, security teams should review and define the correct protection levels and actions that align with their company policies. It is equally important to incorporate alerts into monitoring procedures so that any attempt to modify protected tables is detected promptly.  

By combining these measures, organizations can strengthen compliance, preserve operational transparency, and ensure that sensitive log data remains secure throughout its lifecycle.

---

AI Control Tower is a premium offering that gives enterprises visibility into their AI footprint, manages the AI lifecycle, and identifies risks associated with AI investments. AI Control Tower can help ensure that AI models, workflows, and agents are governed, optimized, and aligned with a customer’s business strategy.

Customers should collaborate with stakeholders to evaluate the need and value of AI Control Tower for their organization. This solution can govern AI assets and manage the lifecycle for both ServiceNow and third-party AI applications.

For more information, refer to the [AI Control Tower documentation](#).

Through the Patching Program, ServiceNow delivers regular updates that include security, performance, and functional fixes to customer instances. ServiceNow enforces an End-of-Life (EOL) policy to ensure that only supported versions receive updates, helping maintain a secure and stable platform for all customers.

### Best practices  

#### Regularly review the ServiceNow security advisories page  
These advisories often highlight vulnerabilities addressed through patches or upgrades, ensuring customers can apply updates promptly to maintain security and compliance. Work with stakeholders, such as the security team, when necessary to apply, mitigate and patch the ServiceNow instance, as needed.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system to review and correlate logs from multiple network and infrastructure sources. A Scheduled Security Operations Checklist is in place, which includes daily reviews of:
- Linux and Windows systems  
- Network devices  
- Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts  
- Behavioral and identified issue logs  

High-risk issues, such as intrusion detection events, trigger real-time alerts that are immediately sent to the Security Incident Response Team for review. Network and infrastructure log events are retained for a minimum of 90 days.

## Security contacts

**Customer responsibility**  
As outlined in the DSA, customers are responsible for identifying and maintaining appropriate security contacts by identifying them in [ServiceNow Support Security Contacts](https://www.servicenow.com).

**Best practices**  

### Create a process to update security contacts regularly  
Ensure the security contact record within ServiceNow Support is always kept up to date, with details of at least two appropriate information security personnel. Set a reminder to review the security contact details at least quarterly to ensure they are current and accurate.  

- Security contacts should be authorized to act on the information they receive, because it may be critically important to the organization.  
- Use a distribution list in the security contact field when possible.

Customers may choose to activate the [ServiceNow access control plugin](#), which enables customers to control which ServiceNow customer service and support employees can access their instance, and when. Review the plugin with stakeholders to determine if it needs to be enabled. Once this control is enabled, ServiceNow personnel must request ad-hoc, time-bound access.

Coordinate with your security and compliance teams to determine the optimal log monitoring approach for your instance. ServiceNow releases two major version updates per year and only supports the current version (N) and one prior release (N-1).

# Data at rest

## Customer responsibility
Data at rest encryption is not enabled by default for customers using the standard ServiceNow Commercial Cloud.

To meet organizational security and compliance requirements, customers must evaluate and implement appropriate encryption solutions for their ServiceNow instance(s).

ServiceNow offers a range of encryption options, including free [Field Encryption Starter](https://example.com) and premium solutions such as [Cloud Encryption (CE)](https://example.com) and [Full Disk Encryption (FDE)](https://example.com), which are available at an additional cost.

Customers are also responsible for key lifecycle management through the [Key Management Framework (KMF)](https://example.com). The KMF introduces specific roles for cryptographic modules and key management operations. Customer admins should review these roles and assign them in accordance with their company’s internal security policy.

If the infrastructure hosting the currently active instance experiences a disruption, ServiceNow activates a failover process that transfers customer operations to the unaffected colocation facility. In this model, the targeted recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) durations are one and two hours, respectively.

### Backups
The ServiceNow [Advanced High Availability (AHA)](https://www.servicenow.com/) architecture is the primary means to restore service in the case of a disruption that could impact availability; however, ServiceNow also performs backups of each customer’s instance(s).

In specific scenarios, using more traditional data backup and recovery mechanisms may be appropriate.

Backups are stored in the same colocation facilities where the data resides, with production instances backed up in both colocation facilities in the pair.

# Data at rest

## Customer responsibility
Data at rest encryption is not enabled by default for customers using the standard ServiceNow Commercial Cloud.

To meet organizational security and compliance requirements, customers must evaluate and implement appropriate encryption solutions for their ServiceNow instance(s).

ServiceNow offers a range of encryption options, including free [Field Encryption Starter](https://example.com) and premium solutions such as [Cloud Encryption (CE)](https://example.com) and [Full Disk Encryption (FDE)](https://example.com), which are available at an additional cost.

Customers are also responsible for key lifecycle management through the [Key Management Framework (KMF)](https://example.com). The KMF introduces specific roles for cryptographic modules and key management operations. Customer admins should review these roles and assign them in accordance with their company’s internal security policy.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>If the infrastructure hosting the currently active instance experiences a disruption, ServiceNow activates a failover process that transfers customer operations to the unaffected colocation facility. In this model, the targeted recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) durations are one and two hours, respectively.

### Backups
The ServiceNow [Advanced High Availability (AHA)](https://www.servicenow.com/) architecture is the primary means to restore service in the case of a disruption that could impact availability; however, ServiceNow also performs backups of each customer’s instance(s).

In specific scenarios, using more traditional data backup and recovery mechanisms may be appropriate.

Backups are stored in the same colocation facilities where the data resides, with production instances backed up in both colocation facilities in the pair.</DOCUMENT>

# RESPOND

## Incident management

### Customer responsibility
During an incident, customers must lead investigations based on their internal processes, security needs, and regulatory obligations, as ServiceNow cannot anticipate these specifics. In addition, ServiceNow asks that customers keep their security contacts updated in the event that ServiceNow needs to reach out for a suspected incident.

While ServiceNow can assist with questions on the investigation, customers are responsible for classifying related behavior as malicious or benign, given their contextual knowledge. [ServiceNow Support](#) can help interpret log samples but cannot review all logs or determine the full scope of an incident.

To ensure effective assistance, customers are responsible for providing detailed information—such as timelines, IPs, and user data—when requesting support. Broad log queries can delay investigations, whereas targeted data enables faster resolution.

### Ensure each user has a unique user account
Ensure that every user is assigned a unique user account within the system. This approach strengthens accountability, enables precise access management, and supports auditing of user activities.

### Machine Identity Console
A machine identity refers to a service account used for inbound API integrations. The Machine Identity Console provides visibility into these identities by listing all accounts with Web Service Access Enabled set to true and/or those that have accessed an API.

These identities are critical for automation, integration, and secure communication, but they’re often invisible and unmanaged. To maintain security and accountability, ensure that individual user accounts are separate from service accounts used for supporting unattended or automation processes.

sentences:
### Manage the organization’s mobile application distribution
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine how to deploy ServiceNow mobile apps securely using an enterprise mobility management (EMM) or mobile application management (MAM) solution. These platforms enforce security policies, manage app configurations, and protect data—even in bring your own device scenarios. ServiceNow supports distribution through common EMM or mobile device management (MDM) platforms.

### Conduct Mobile Application Penetration Testing
Determine whether a mobile application penetration test is needed by collaborating with your security team and ServiceNow instance administrator. Under the Customer Penetration Testing Policy, customers may conduct regular penetration tests on their organization’s ServiceNow mobile applications to identify potential security risks.

---

---

## Best practices

### Choose an encryption method for data at rest in an instance*
The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

Based on this assessment, customers should select the most appropriate encryption method offered by ServiceNow. When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

### Customers seeking included functionality
**Field Encryption Starter**:  
Data stored within a ServiceNow instance can be protected with Field Encryption Starter, which allows customers to encrypt specific fields within the instance using AES128 or AES256 encryption.

#### Address noncompliance with security hardening and hardening compliance score
Use [Security hardening](https://www.servicenow.com) to identify, test, and assess noncompliance in a sub-production instance. Review the hardening compliance score to determine how closely your instance aligns with SSC hardening recommendations.

*Note: A high compliance score does not guarantee that the instance is fully secure—it only reflects alignment with SSC hardening settings.*

#### Run Security Center security scans regularly
The [Security scanner](https://www.servicenow.com) helps discover and correct access control misconfigurations. Use the Security Scanner built-in to SSC to scan your instance against a set of security checks in order to identify misconfigurations on a regular cadence.

Administrators should collaborate closely with their organization’s security teams to define the appropriate scope and duration for any scheduled penetration tests. Once testing is complete, administrators and security personnel must coordinate to review any findings, prioritize remediation efforts, and establish clear timelines to address findings.

# Mobile application security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for implementing and maintaining security measures that protect their ServiceNow mobile environment. This includes enforcing strong authentication methods such as MFA, managing user privileges, and configuring mobile security settings to align with the organizational policies and standards.

---

## Best practices

### Configure mobile application security controls
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine the configuration of built-in mobile security controls. This process should include reviewing the following controls to ensure alignment with organizational policies and standards: clipboard restrictions, disabling screenshots, preventing attachments, requiring an in-app PIN, and enabling background blur.

- **Now Assist Admin Console:** Configure, monitor, and troubleshoot Now Assist applications and skills. This includes assigning models at the skill level, tracking usage, and providing visibility into system behavior.
- **Now Assist Skill Kit:** Equip developers with tools to build and evaluate custom generative AI skills.
- **Now Assist Data Kit:** Enable developers to manage datasets and create evaluation collections to support custom skill development and testing workflows.
- **AI Agent Studio:** Offer a no-code interface for designing and managing AI Agents. Developers can define roles, assign tools, and connect agents to existing workflows using natural language configuration.
```

### Monitor email and malware metrics
Collaborate with stakeholders to establish effective monitoring of email and anti-malware activity. Configure alerts to proactively identify abnormal email activity or potential malware threats and have documented mitigation measures. There are metrics available in the ServiceNow Security Center (SSC) to review.

### Encrypt email with TLS and S/MIME
ServiceNow mail infrastructure is designed to use opportunistic TLS to encrypt email in transit. Ensure the organization’s sending and receiving email infrastructure supports this setting.

ServiceNow also supports the Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) standard. S/MIME is an end-to-end encryption protocol for sending digitally signed and encrypted emails, ensuring data confidentiality, authenticity, and integrity. Collaborate with stakeholders to determine if this feature should be configured.

Customers should also work with all stakeholders to set the prioritization of each best practice.

ServiceNow stands ready to provide guidance and support once you’ve begun implementing these measures. Work with your account teams or open a [ServiceNow Support](https://www.servicenow.com) case for more clarification.

# Best practices continued

## Enhanced protective controls

### Implement Data Privacy for Now Assist
Engage stakeholders to assess the need and value of enabling [Data Privacy for Now Assist](#). This solution integrates with the [Generative AI Controller](#) and uses real-time anonymization with configurable data patterns to protect sensitive information before prompts are submitted to the LLM.

### Enable Now Assist Guardian for enhanced protection
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine whether Now Assist Guardian is needed to safeguard users and data. This feature monitors LLM requests and responses to detect offensive or harmful content, prompt injection attempts, and filtered topics. Offensive content and injection attempts can be logged or blocked based on your configuration. If a filter is triggered, users are redirected to the Sensitivity Detection: Fallback topic in Virtual Agent.

For detailed implementation guidance, refer to the [Now Assist Guardian](#) documentation.

#### Periodically review the ServiceNow Customer Security Portal
Establish a process to conduct regular reviews of the Customer Security Portal, including compliance certifications, security advisories, Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs), SOC reports, and instance security best practices. Whether evaluating ServiceNow as a vendor or seeking guidance on instance security, this portal serves as a centralized resource for all ServiceNow security needs.

---

### Additional information
- [Video: ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal](#)
- [ServiceNow Customer Security Portal](#)
- [Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) STAR Level 1 (CAIQ and EU Cloud) and Level 2 (STAR Certification)](#)

The links below require access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#).
- [Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT)](#)
- [Standardized Information Gathering (SIG) questionnaire](#)
- [ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal Directory](#)

---

#### Understand your organization’s incident response escalation channels
One of the most important variables during a security incident is the time between the incident being reported and when your security team is alerted. To minimize this time as much as possible, ensure that you understand the appropriate contacts within your organization that need to be alerted when an incident is reported. This could be an email address, a catalog item within your internal resources, or a post to a messaging channel. By understanding the initial steps to be taken, customers will be able to quickly respond to an incident, whether it is reported by a company resource or by [ServiceNow Support](#) cases or COMM records.

# ServiceNow Security Center
## Secure instance configuration

### Customer responsibility
Users can monitor the [ServiceNow Security Center (SSC)](https://www.servicenow.com) to review hardening settings, security scanner outcomes, and metrics related to instance security. Customers are required to prioritize hardening configuration options in Security Center according to their organization’s requirements.

### Best practices

#### Establish security hardening priorities
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to develop a comprehensive hardening plan related to a ServiceNow instance that aligns with the organization’s security strategy and priorities. Create a process to apply the plan to a ServiceNow instance using the security hardening setting in ServiceNow Security Center.

## Understand the difference between Allow-If and Deny-Unless ACLs
Allow-If allows access upon successful evaluation and is the default ACL. Deny-Unless denies access unless there is a successful evaluation. Deny-Unless ACLs will take priority against Allow-If ACLs in ACL Evaluation as it will be evaluated first. The Deny-Unless ACL defines the users that will NOT be denied. Said another way, the user will be denied access unless the role, condition, and script requirements are met.

## Verify Security Jump Start—ACL Rules Plugin is enabled
All new ServiceNow instances have the [Security Jump Start—ACL Rules plugin](#) installed to provide a base level of access security for key system tables. Use this plugin to establish foundational ACL protections for sensitive system data.

#### Classify data in the instance
Data classification is available to all customers and enables the identification and classification of stored data for each instance, ensuring that data controls meet organizational requirements, as agreed by the stakeholders.

Data classification is for data that is known. Data discovery allows the discovery of data in comment fields, description fields, or attachments. Data anonymization can be used to mitigate issues and limit risk.

#### Allocate roles within the instance according to data access requirements
Identify which individuals are authorized to access data according to its classification, document these permissions, and establish roles that align with expected access requirements.

- **REST API**: Admin can define a global API auth policy or API specific auth policy.

<DOCUMENT>The assessment typically spans several months and follows an iterative process where findings are remediated by ServiceNow security and development teams. Results of these penetration tests are available to customers and prospects under NDA via the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal.

## Best practices

### Create a process to examine ServiceNow penetration test reports periodically
Create a process to ensure stakeholders, such as your security team, review the most recent published [ServiceNow penetration test reports](#) on the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#).</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>All inbound email to the ServiceNow AI Platform is analyzed for malware and SPAM scoring. Malware scanning is performed using **ServiceNow Antivirus Protection**. X-headers are added to messages to reflect the results of this analysis, and customers can interpret and act on these headers using the **Email Filter plugin**. If a malicious email or attachment is detected, it is quarantined in the instance for inspection.

### Leverage the existing organization’s email infrastructure
If the organization already has a mature email security environment, consider using that infrastructure through the **Advanced Email Setup** features.

Customers can integrate their own email infrastructure and security gateways to control how mail to and from the instance is processed. A ServiceNow instance supports integration via SMTP, POP3, and IMAP, and can also read email using Microsoft Graph to connect with Microsoft Exchange Online.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>Administrators should collaborate closely with their organization’s security teams to define the appropriate scope and duration for any scheduled penetration tests. Once testing is complete, administrators and security personnel must coordinate to review any findings, prioritize remediation efforts, and establish clear timelines to address findings.

## Understand access by ServiceNow personnel
Collaborate closely with stakeholders to ensure everyone is informed about the circumstances under which ServiceNow personnel may access customer data. Access is restricted to designated customer support employees assigned to open support cases and is only granted with explicit customer authorization. All such access is temporary, tightly controlled, and fully auditable. Customers are encouraged to actively monitor their instance event logs and use the Security Center widget to review access events, ensuring full transparency and reinforcing trust in the security of their data. Customers can identify this activity at any time by tracking the occurrence of the identifier name@snc in the instance event logs.

```markdown
# Mobile application security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for implementing and maintaining security measures that protect their ServiceNow mobile environment. This includes enforcing strong authentication methods such as MFA, managing user privileges, and configuring mobile security settings to align with the organizational policies and standards.

---

## Best practices

### Configure mobile application security controls
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine the configuration of built-in mobile security controls. This process should include reviewing the following controls to ensure alignment with organizational policies and standards: clipboard restrictions, disabling screenshots, preventing attachments, requiring an in-app PIN, and enabling background blur.

```markdown
# The Shared Responsibility Model

Security is a partnership between ServiceNow and the customer, both with specific responsibilities. Therefore, it is essential that each party understands their role in this partnership. Using the extensive capabilities of the ServiceNow AI Platform, customers can configure instances to meet their unique security policies and obligations while also complying with any regional or industry-specific requirements.

- **As the data controller**, the customer determines access rights to their instance and the data it contains. Security controls within the instance enable customers to implement policies appropriate to their own requirements and make decisions on data classification.

- **As the data processor**, ServiceNow secures the platform infrastructure and provides tools for security management and monitoring according to customer requirements.

- Decide between agent-less, agent-based, or hybrid access.
- Establish a credential management strategy (Credentials table or External Credentials Storage — i.e., CyberArk).
- The Windows MID Server uses the login credentials of the MID Server service by default.
- For non-admin access, consider [Microsoft Just Enough Administration (JEA)](#) for basic discovery. For agent-based access, use [ServiceNow Agent Client Collector (ACC)](#) and configure allow lists to restrict commands.
- For Linux and UNIX machines and network devices, the MID Server uses the SSH and SNMP credentials configured on the instance.
- MID Servers can be configured to perform mutual authentication with the ServiceNow instance, employing a TLS client certificate for authentication. Customers use TLS certificates for mutual authentication.

---

*November 2025 | Release: Zurich*

# Request that the support case be marked as a security case
If a case being submitted involves confirmed compromise of customer information, customers are able to request the case be flagged as a security case, which limits the case visibility as needed. Ensure that security cases are intentionally designated as such. Customer visibility into a security case is limited to the submitter and any accounts designated on the case’s watchlist.

## Educate your security team on how to raise a case with ServiceNow Support
Ensure that your security team, or at a minimum, the designated security contact in [Security Contacts on ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com), has documentation on how to create a support case via [support.servicenow.com](https://support.servicenow.com) in the event they need to report an incident and cannot contact a member of the platform team.

```markdown
# Best practices continued

## Integrate MFA with existing IdPs
Enable MFA with your existing IdP to strengthen account security. Additionally, customer admins can require high-privileged users to authenticate with FIDO2 authenticators that use stronger methods, passwordless devices, or biometrics, ensuring more protection for sensitive actions.

Customers can also allow low-privileged users to authenticate with an email one-time password (OTP) or a short message service (SMS) OTP. These methods are easy to use and require minimal setup.

## Review the MFA dashboard
Use the MFA Dashboard to gain MFA insights such as user enrollment, privileged admins who haven’t opted in to MFA, and compliance. To enhance instance security, the MFA dashboard will help customer admins confirm that all users have enabled MFA.

### Consider additional restriction policies
Customers can implement [cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS) rules to control which domains can access specific REST API endpoints. Adaptive Authentication policies can be applied specifically to APIs, restricting both the API endpoint and the web methods employed. ACLs can be required for scripted APIs. An API access policy sets permissions and access duration, allowing you to control inbound ServiceNow API access according to authentication type and filter criteria.
